title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang wants ‘no incidents’ of AI cybersecurity, and says AI doomers ‘ought to stop working on’ the technology
key_facts: Jensen Huang, Nvidia chief executive, told Fortune in London the industry should accept no AI-caused cybersecurity incidents.
Earlier this month Sam Altman, OpenAI chief executive, told Vanity Fair some hacks and scams may be a necessary trade-off for AI's benefits.
Altman later told Politico's Decoded podcast of 'a coming tidal wave of cybersecurity problems' from rival open-source models.
Huang said incidents so far could have been avoided with stronger containment and monitoring of AI agents, like browsers isolating websites.
Huang shrugged off existential-risk warnings, including from Anthropic's Dario Amodei, saying the technology is 'completely in our control'.
Huang said Nvidia would announce $2 billion in new European investments within a week, on top of $8 billion already committed.
quote_evidence: "I'm willing to accept no incidents of cybersecurity. We should not accept any of them," he told Fortune in an interview in London.
"I don't know why anybody would want to support the advancement of a technology that's going to result, you know, in the end of human civilization as we know it."
why_it_matters_hint: A public disagreement between Nvidia's and OpenAI's chief executives over what AI harm is acceptable.
notes: Reply story: Huang answers Altman's Vanity Fair and Politico Decoded remarks (dates of those interviews given only as 'earlier this month' and 'subsequent'). Not previously carried in our editions as far as the 14 Oct title list shows.
